name: DHT22
full_name: DHT22 / AM2302 Digital Temperature and Humidity Sensor
description: Calibrated digital sensor that reports both relative humidity and temperature over a proprietary single-wire serial protocol. It contains a capacitive humidity element and a thermistor with an onboard MCU that outputs a 40-bit frame. It runs from 3.3 to 6 V and offers better range and accuracy than the cheaper DHT11. The single-wire data line is open-drain style and needs a pull-up; the sensor must not be polled faster than once every 2 seconds.

pins.name: DATA
pins.description: single-wire serial data I/O; requires external pull-up (4.7k-10k)

typical_application: Indoor environmental monitoring (room temperature and humidity logging, HVAC, weather stations) connected to a single MCU GPIO.
gotchas: DATA needs a pull-up resistor (typically 4.7k to 10k) to VDD; many breakout boards include one but bare sensors do not
do not sample faster than once every 2 seconds or readings become unreliable
raw 4-pin pinout is VDD, DATA, NC, GND; 3-pin breakout boards omit the NC pin and reorder, so check the board silkscreen
the protocol is bit-banged timing-critical; not I2C despite the single data line
allow ~1-2 s after power-up before the first read while the sensor stabilizes
long cable runs degrade signal integrity; keep wiring short or add a stronger pull-up
